meta.title: The Treasury’s Gold Revaluation Play | Lyn Alden
meta.speakers: Lyn Alden (investment strategist, author), Wealthion host
meta.thread_line: 6 threads · fiscal dominance · Treasury gold revaluation · AI buildout risk · gold-and-stocks positioning · a two-speed economy · Orange Juice permanent-capital model

snapshot: Lyn Alden's core frame: we are in **fiscal dominance**, not monetary dominance; deficits now create more new money than bank lending, so Fed rate tools are aimed at the wrong channel.

A Treasury **gold revaluation** is one of the few 'break the glass' ways to create money without debt; she says it's worth monitoring, would be inflationary and good for asset holders, bad for wage holders.
AI buildout: she sees valid questions (lease obligations, vendor financing, GPU depreciation, unprofitable labs) but thinks we're in early-to-mid innings and **a reckoning is later, not now**.
She owns both gold and stocks: 'being bearish on stocks basically means you're bullish on fiat'; she fades both the equity-bear and the gold-only doomer narratives.
AI is a small share of commodity demand; defense spending adds demand while China's peak demographics and oversupply weigh on it.
Biggest worries: demographics, fiscal deficits, geopolitics and a K-shaped economy with record stock prices alongside weak consumer sentiment.
Her new venture, Orange Juice, buys small and mid-size cash-flow businesses as permanent capital (Berkshire-style) with a Bitcoin treasury as a second avenue.

themes.title: Fiscal dominance: deficits now drive money creation, so Fed tools miss
themes.lead: Annual deficits now exceed net new bank loans plus corporate bonds, so rate policy is solving a different problem.
bullets: Fed tools (rates, balance sheet) work through the bank-lending channel, which drove money growth in Paul Volcker's era but is now smaller than the deficit channel.
Net new Treasuries issued over 12 months are bigger than the sum of net new bank loans and net new corporate bond issuance.
Higher rates also raise the deficit, and cash-rich holders (money market funds, locked-in mortgages, her own company's capital) get 'a raise' when the Fed hikes.
At roughly **100% debt-to-GDP**, the question is how the Fed communicates it isn't its purview; central banks are built around the idea that they can solve this.
Energy matters: a war ending and refineries no longer being hit would mildly lower inflation, but the K-shaped economy and above-target inflation predate the war.
AI power and resource demand also crowd out homebuilding, keeping home prices high despite higher rates.
'When does the debt matter?' She says it has been mattering: the cost lands on non-recipients like a family buying a first home.

quote.text: When does the debt matter? My answer is it has been mattering.

themes.status: TREASURY OPTION, NOT AN ANNOUNCED PLAN
themes.title: Revaluing Treasury gold is a 'break the glass' lever
themes.lead: Marking the official gold stock to market would fill the Treasury General Account with spendable cash without issuing debt.
bullets: The host cites Bessent's recent counselors (including Judy Shelton, a known sound-money figure) and Hank Paulson calling this a 'break the glass' moment as fuel for speculation.
Mechanism: official books carry gold at 40-something dollars an ounce; revaluing to roughly $4,000+ an ounce creates cash the Treasury can spend until it's used up.
It's mostly an accounting trick at first, but spending the cash is pro-liquidity and inflationary, comparable to post-COVID stimulus depending on magnitude.
Winners: gold, equity and Bitcoin holders (scarce assets); losers: wage earners years later, unless offset by fiscal policy beneficial to them.
Trade-off: it weakens the dollar (if that's the intent) but also hits wages; every lever helps one group and hurts another, so officials may kick it to the next team.
themes.watch: She says only that it's 'worth monitoring'; the host raised the idea and no policy move has been announced.

names.name: Gold
names.blurb: Revaluation of official holdings would be a shock that likely pushes people toward gold.

themes.title: AI buildout: valid red flags, but the reckoning is later
themes.lead: Lease obligations and circular financing are real risks; she doesn't put them in subprime territory yet.
bullets: Hyperscalers are taking on increasing long-term lease obligations; chipmakers help raise funds and backstop data-center buildouts (vendor financing, a circular structure).
Frontier labs are chased by open-weight models: 'very hard to justify a trillion or two trillion dollar valuation' while aggressively unprofitable and only months ahead of copiers.
Things outside the banking system tend to be less catastrophic than subprime; she expects pretty big drawdowns at certain points.
Her indicator: are businesses spending more or less on AI than months ago; headlines of pullbacks keep appearing while aggregate spend keeps rising.
Studies show higher AI adopters win share and often *increase headcount*; open question is useful life of a leading-edge GPU.
Open source: she says trying to ban open-weight competitors through regulation is 'whack-a-mole' and a losing game; open models let more than a few companies control the tech.
themes.watch: Host framed the AI-contract risk as bigger than subprime; Alden disagreed with that scale. She invests in venture and public markets, so she has exposure to the trade she discusses.

names.name: OpenAI, Anthropic
names.blurb: Valuation questions: unprofitable and only months ahead of closest copiers.

themes.title: Own gold and equities: fiat debasement favors scarce assets
themes.lead: She sees commodities and scarce assets in a bull market and fades the doomers on both sides.
bullets: Bullish gold (it 'got ahead of its keys' for a while but is on track long term), silver, potentially platinum, copper, and energy assets; she also invests in Brazil, where owning its biggest bank has outperformed the index.
S&P 500 to gold ratio: in the fourth major bear market for stocks relative to gold in a century, though a mild one. Gold going from 2000 to 5000 quickly needs a breather.
'Being bearish on stocks basically means you're bullish on fiat'; with deficits at 7% of GDP 'as far as the eye can see'.

Since COVID the winners have been gold, Bitcoin, quality equities and best real estate with fixed-rate debt; bonds had one of the worst five-or-six year stretches, and a lot of that move is probably over.
AI is a small share of global commodity use; defense (US asking for a **$1.5 trillion** defense budget, Europe spending more) adds demand; China's peak demographics and oversupply weigh on it.
Public markets: she wants profitable growth (semiconductor companies are 'incredibly profitable'); unprofitable growth belongs in venture.

themes.watch: She publishes a transparent model portfolio in her newsletter and runs a venture fund and an acquisition company, so her positions overlap with these views.

names.name: Bitcoin (BTC)
names.blurb: Scarce-asset winner since COVID; Orange Juice holds a Bitcoin treasury.

themes.title: Demographics, a K-shaped economy and algorithmic trust erosion
themes.lead: These problems come in clusters; the two-tier economy can last longer than people think but risks breaking toward the extremes.
bullets: Demographics: systems assume each generation is bigger; six workers per retiree vs three; Social Security, Medicare, Japan, Europe and China are all exposed.
Geopolitics shifting from unipolar back toward multipolar, with breakdowns in international law.
Record high stock prices alongside record low consumer sentiment: a divide between asset holders and deficit recipients versus non-asset holders and non-recipients.
The aristocracy sustained such divides for a very long time, but the risk is horseshoe politics; the host notes the midterms as a test.
A handful of big platforms tune algorithms for profit or other aims; she and Jack Dorsey discussed choosing your own algorithm via decentralized social media.
Video as proof and trust in institutions have fallen, so people shrink their world back to local; her sci-fi imagines a centralized censored internet plus edges.
AI as equalizer: it's never been easier to start a small business, if you avoid 'AI brain'.

themes.title: Orange Juice: a Berkshire-style permanent-capital buyer with a Bitcoin treasury
themes.lead: It buys small and mid-size businesses to hold indefinitely, pitched as the alternative to private equity's flip-it playbook.
bullets: She says it's not a Bitcoin treasury company but a company that has a Bitcoin treasury as part of its strategy.
Private equity critique: buy, leverage on cheap debt, cut staff, flip in a few years; a 10-year fund mandate pulls profits forward and it ends with a larger-than-average failure rate.
Permanent capital (Berkshire Hathaway is the example, funded by insurance) is geared to decades of cash flows; Bitcoin on the balance sheet can be 'rocket fuel' if managed appropriately.
Sellers: owners who like Bitcoin and want a legacy, and owners who want liquidity but keep working; hundreds of companies have reached out.
A new CTO hired from Nvidia advises acquired firms on AI to reduce busy work, not cut back-end staff.
Counter-cyclical edge: pure Bitcoin-treasury companies like Strategy tend to buy Bitcoin at highs and can't raise capital in bear markets; Orange Juice can lean on its acquisition funnel instead.
themes.watch: Alden is a founder of this company and its capital sits in interest-bearing fiat; this is her own pitch, not an outside view.

names.name: Strategy (MSTR)
names.blurb: Pure Bitcoin-treasury company with pro-cyclical accumulation.

names.name: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B)
names.blurb: Model for a permanent capital vehicle with an insurance float.

takeaways.title: Track net new Treasury issuance against bank lending to see where money growth actually comes from
Monitor any Treasury move on gold holdings; it is a debt-free liquidity lever
Watch whether businesses spend more or less on AI each quarter, not single-company pullback headlines
Hold scarce assets and profitable equities together instead of choosing a doomer or bull tribe
Net AI, defense and China demand against each other before sizing a commodity position
Compare permanent-capital buyers against private equity before selling a small business

glossary.def: A regime where government deficits, not bank lending, are the main source of new money, so central bank rate tools lose potency.
Marking the Treasury's official gold holdings from the old book price to market price, creating cash in the Treasury General Account.
A company that buys businesses and holds them indefinitely instead of flipping them on a fund timeline.
An economy where asset holders and deficit recipients diverge from everyone else.
